# TasteForge Video

Curated by Skill Harbor: documents ECC's packaged offline engine and its strict evidence contract for taste-driven video work. TasteForge turns "make it feel like this reference" into a repeatable, inspectable workflow: interview taste, distill it into a structured style pack, validate the pack against schemas, apply its measured cadence and look to local media, and export an editable, frame-exact timeline. The canonical implementation is the `tasteforge` package shipped inside ECC; for the complete standalone creative pipeline, use `taste-distillation` then `taste-application` first. The core boundary is what makes this skill: operations are local, deterministic and offline (taste interview to profile, pack inspection and validation, dry-run distillation with measured grounding, cut planning from measured cadence, EDL/FCPXML export to DaVinci Resolve, Premiere or Final Cut), and planning fails closed before any provider generation. Also covers generated-media provenance audits: where a pack, spec or cut came from, what was measured locally versus generated by a provider, what was dry-run. Use for file-driven multimodal image, video and 3D-asset discovery, style-pack validation, and offline planning that must fail closed. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: the deterministic part is planning and structure; actual footage generation still needs provider tools, and the skill is explicit about that...
